gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Huawei's own compatibility table for the Watch D2 marks cuff blood-pressure measurement and 24-hour ambulatory BP (ABPM) as supported on iPhone (iOS 13.0+), the same as on Android, and that both airbag strap sizes come in the box: M for 130–160 mm wrists, L for 161–210 mm. For comparison, Samsung's BP needs a Galaxy phone, and Apple's hypertension notifications show no readings and leave out Apple Watch SE.
standout_why: Compared against the cited rivals news.samsung.com (Galaxy Watch4+, Galaxy phone on Android 12, 28-day cuff calibration: already covered), us.hilo.com blog (says nothing on phone OS) and cardilog.app (would not load because of a TLS error). Also checked top results: fitcoin.co says only that the Huawei D3's 'phone integration is weakest on iPhone and the cuff readings do not land in Apple's blood pressure log', and gives no strap or wrist ranges. gadget-hub.jp says Huawei Health was pulled from Google Play but is still on the App Store. Two cited rivals, androidauthority.com and wareable.com, returned 403 and could not be read. None of the pages I read says that the D2's BP and ABPM features are fully supported on iOS, or gives the M/L airbag wrist ranges.
decides: ChatGPT ended by asking 'Which phone do you use?', and this finding answers that. For iPhone users who want real mmHg readings, the Huawei Watch D2/D3 is the only cuff watch here whose maker lists BP and 24-hour BP as working on iOS. It is still an import with no FDA clearance and no US warranty. Apple Watch gives only hypertension alerts, on Series 9+/Ultra 2+ and not SE, so Dealectric's listed Apple Watch SE 3 gets no BP feature at all. Galaxy Watch BP works only with a Galaxy phone, and only on a watch and phone bought in the US. Dealectric's listed Galaxy Watch 8 qualifies under that rule. Android users on non-Samsung phones get Huawei Health from AppGallery, not Google Play. Hilo Core needs iOS 16+ or Android 14+.

findings.label: BP measurement and 24-hour BP (ABPM) on iPhone
findings.value: Supported on iOS 13.0 or later and Android 8.0 or later (both ticked for 'Blood pressure measurement', '24-hour BP' and 'BP fluctuation feedback')
findings.source_title: Compatibility of the HUAWEI WATCH D2 and Android/iOS Phones
findings.note: Huawei's feature table. ECG, arterial stiffness and sleep apnea are also ticked for iOS but marked 'some countries/regions'.

findings.label: Features unavailable on iPhone
findings.value: Quick SMS/app replies, third-party call notifications, local music, Wallet bank cards, AI Voice, watch AppGallery, screenshots
findings.source_title: Compatibility of the HUAWEI WATCH D2 and Android/iOS Phones
findings.note: All are marked ✗ for iOS in the same table. None of them is a health feature.

findings.label: Wrist fit / airbag straps
findings.value: Wrists 130–210 mm: M airbag strap 130–160 mm, L airbag strap 161–210 mm; both in the box (L fitted)
findings.note: Box contents: 'Device (with an L-sized airbag strap and short strap) × 1' and 'M-sized airbag strap × 1'.

findings.label: Phone OS and wrist fit
findings.value: Android 8.0+ / iOS 13.0+; wrists 130–210 mm (M 130–160 mm, L 161–210 mm, both in the box); strap width 25.5 mm
findings.note: The specs page has no per-feature iOS table, so for the D3 I could only check BP-on-iOS against the D2 table.

findings.label: Strap compatibility
findings.value: Only Huawei straps fit, because of the pump and its special connectors; one case size
findings.source_title: Notebookcheck: Huawei Watch D2 Smartwatch review
findings.note: Notebookcheck also says ECG, BP measurement and sleep breathing monitoring need a Huawei ID, and that iOS restrictions 'do not affect the health functions'.

findings.label: US app availability
findings.value: Huawei Health removed from Google Play in 2023 (Android users install via AppGallery); still on Apple's App Store
findings.source_title: Can You Buy a HUAWEI Watch in the US? (2026 Guide)
findings.note: Same page: no FDA clearance found for the D2's BP feature, and parallel imports have no US Huawei warranty.

findings.product: Samsung Galaxy Watch (Watch4 and later, incl. Watch8/Watch9)
findings.label: BP feature requirements
findings.value: Galaxy Watch4 or later (Galaxy Fit excluded) on Wear OS 4.0+, paired with a Galaxy smartphone on Android 12+; calibrate with an upper-arm cuff (sold separately) every 28 days
findings.source_title: Samsung Health Monitor | Apps & Services | Samsung US
findings.note: Calibration takes 3 cuff readings within 30 minutes. Measurement range 70–180 / 40–120 mmHg; calibration range 80–170 / 50–110 mmHg. 'For wellness only'.

findings.label: Region lock
findings.value: Samsung Health Monitor works only on watches and smartphones purchased in the country/region where the service is available; US rollout began 2026-03-31
findings.source_title: Samsung's Blood Pressure Monitoring Feature Now Available to U.S. Users in Samsung Health | Samsung Mobile Press
findings.note: From footnotes 1, 4 and 12 of the release.

findings.label: Model/phone eligibility
findings.value: Apple Watch Series 9 or later or Ultra 2 or later on the latest watchOS, paired with iPhone 11 or later; not available on Apple Watch SE; user must be 22+, not pregnant and without a hypertension diagnosis; Wrist Detection on
findings.source_title: Hypertension notifications on your Apple Watch - Apple Support
findings.note: Alerts only; the page gives no mmHg readings. So Dealectric's listed Apple Watch SE 3 is excluded.

findings.label: Regional exclusion
findings.value: Hypertension notifications 'may not be available on Apple Watch Series 12 or Ultra 4' in 26 footnoted regions (e.g., Japan, India, South Korea, UAE) pending regulatory clearances; the United States is not footnoted
findings.note: Read from footnote 7 and the list of footnoted countries.

findings.label: Phone requirements
findings.value: iOS 16 or later or Android 14 or later, Bluetooth 5.0 or later; tablets and desktop computers not supported
findings.source_title: Does my phone support the Hilo app? | Hilo Core support
findings.note: Hilo's own blog (cited by ChatGPT) gives the cuff recalibration interval as 30 days and says the band and system are not FDA-cleared; only the cuff is.
